name: Wikimedia Enterprise docs
description: Wikimedia Enterprise API docs: search the guides, read every endpoint. Read-only, no account needed.
author: Wikimedia Enterprise

tools.name: search
tools.title: Search the Wikimedia Enterprise docs
tools.description: Full-text search over the Wikimedia Enterprise API documentation: guide sections, the changelog, pricing, endpoints and response models. Exact tokens work best (a field name such as `reference_risk_score`, a status code such as `429`, or a path such as `/v2/snapshots/{identifier}/download`); plain questions work too. Returns ids to pass to `fetch`.

query.description: What to look for. Field names, endpoint paths, status codes and plain questions all work.

scope.description: `docs` for the prose guides, `reference` for endpoints and models, `all` for both.

tools.name: fetch
tools.title: Fetch a docs page, endpoint or model
tools.description: Full text for one id from `search`: `docs/<slug>` (a guide, as markdown; a `#section` suffix is accepted; `docs/changelog` is the release notes and `docs/pricing` the plans), `op/<operationId>` (one endpoint rendered from the OpenAPI definition) or `schema/<name>` (one response model).

tools.name: list_endpoints
tools.title: List API endpoints
tools.description: Every endpoint in the Wikimedia Enterprise OpenAPI definition, in reference order, with its technical title, its plain-language line and a link into the reference. Filter with a tag: authentication, codes, languages, projects, namespaces, batches, wikidata-batches, snapshots, wikidata-snapshots, structured-snapshots, articles, structured-contents, wikidata, realtime-articles, realtime-wikidata.

tag.description: An OpenAPI tag; omit for all endpoints.

tools.name: get_endpoint
tools.title: Get one endpoint
tools.description: The exact request and response shape of one endpoint, dereferenced from the OpenAPI definition (the source of truth), as structured JSON plus a markdown rendering. Identify it by `operationId`, or by `method` and `path`.

path.description: Templated path as written in the reference, e.g. `/v2/snapshots/{identifier}`

resources.name: docs-agents
resources.title: AI Agents and MCP
resources.description: How coding agents and AI assistants read this documentation: the llms.txt index, markdown versions of every guide, and the docs MCP server with its four tools.

resources.name: docs-authentication
resources.title: Authentication
resources.description: Use credentials and tokens to manage your Wikimedia Enterprise account programmatically. Covers login, token refresh, token revoke, and password management endpoints.

resources.name: docs-best-practices
resources.title: Best Practices
resources.description: Practical guidance on authentication, fields, filters, and efficient use of the Snapshot, On-demand, and Realtime Wikimedia Enterprise APIs.

resources.name: docs-credibility-signals
resources.title: Tuning Credibility Signals
resources.description: How to put credibility signals to work in your pipeline: recommended thresholds, an evaluation strategy, and field-by-field reference tables.

resources.name: docs-data-dictionary
resources.title: Data Model and Data Dictionary
resources.description: How a Wikimedia Enterprise API response is shaped: the article object at its center, the parsed and Wikidata variants beside it, and where every field is defined.

resources.name: docs-data-primer
resources.title: Wikimedia Data Primer
resources.description: What are the differences between Wikimedia, Wikipedia, and MediaWiki? Who writes and edits all these articles? What API should I use to access article content?

resources.name: docs-filtering
resources.title: Fields, Filters, and Limit
resources.description: Use fields, filters, and limit POST parameters to customize what the Wikimedia Enterprise API returns - scope by project, language, namespace, or field.

resources.name: docs-identifiers
resources.title: Identifiers
resources.description: The format each Wikimedia Enterprise API resource expects for its identifier - snapshot bundles, chunks, hourly batches, projects, languages, namespaces - and how to look up valid values.

resources.name: docs-index
resources.title: Getting Started
resources.description: Sign up for a free account, get your JWT tokens, and make your first calls to the Wikimedia Enterprise Snapshot, On-demand, and Realtime APIs.

resources.name: docs-metadata
resources.title: Metadata
resources.description: Reference endpoints for project codes, languages, projects, and namespaces used across the Wikimedia Enterprise API to build accurate queries.

resources.name: docs-on-demand
resources.title: On-demand API
resources.description: REST API returning the current version of any article from all supported Wikimedia projects by name, with optional metadata filtering and field selection.

resources.name: docs-realtime
resources.title: Realtime API
resources.description: Stream real-time Wikimedia article and Wikidata updates via SSE or NDJSON, or download hourly batch files of changes across all supported projects, including Wikidata.

resources.name: docs-snapshot
resources.title: Snapshot API
resources.description: Download every article in a Wikimedia project as compressed NDJSON files. Free monthly snapshots included; daily updates and chunk downloads also available.

resources.name: docs-status-codes
resources.title: Status Codes
resources.description: Overview of HTTP response status codes returned by the Wikimedia Enterprise APIs, including success, redirection, client error, and server error codes.

resources.name: docs-pricing
resources.title: Wikimedia Enterprise API Pricing
resources.description: Wikipedia API pricing: compare free and paid Wikimedia Enterprise accounts for Wikipedia and Wikidata data at scale. Start with a free account, no credit card.

resources.name: openapi
resources.title: OpenAPI definition
resources.description: The Wikimedia Enterprise API, OpenAPI 3.1. The source of truth for every request and response shape.
